item.title: Silanols in zeolite catalysis: from defects to designable functionality
item.description:
Authors: Ye Ding, Fuyuan Hao, Jiachun Su, Xutong Meng, Mei-Yan Wang, Ji Qi, Shouying Huang, Xinbin Ma

Zeolite silanols were long treated mainly as structural defects, but recent catalytic studies show that specific silanol populations can also function as catalytically relevant sites or local environments.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00169f

item.title: In-field crop disease surveillance: from phenotypes to molecules
item.description:
Authors: Xuhan Xia, Ting Zhang, Qiuyu Luo, Honghong Wu, Qingshan Wei, Ruijie Deng

This review outlines crop pathogen biomarkers and in-field molecular detection advances, evaluates in-field tool readiness, and details their applications in early disease detection, field pathogen survey, pesticide guidance, and mechanism research.

DOI: 10.1039/d5cs01551k

item.title: Monolayer molecular crystals: controlled-growth technologies, structure–property relationships, and device applications
item.description:
Authors: Yuanyuan Zhang, Daowei He, Tao Zhang, Guocai Liu, Chengliang Wang, Lang Jiang

This review establishes a mechanism-driven framework for monolayer molecular crystals (MMCs), integrating controlled growth, structure–property relationships, and device applications. It outlines pathways toward scalable molecular electronics.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01235c

item.title: Electrochemical conversion of low-concentration carbon dioxide to multicarbon products: advances, challenges, and perspectives
item.description:
Authors: Xuanzhao Lu, Chen Qin, Jingyao Xia, Baozhen Yuan, Tangrui Li, Chen Zhou, Yujing Jiang, Ao Xia, Bing Song, Richen Lin, Wenlei Zhu

This review highlights advances in electrochemical conversion of low-concentration CO 2 to multicarbon products, covering dilute and impurity-containing CO 2 , capture-solution electrolysis, bioelectrocatalysis, and techno-economic analysis.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00916f

item.title: Hydrogen borrowing with heterogeneous catalysis
item.description:
Authors: Karel Weemaes, Robby Vroemans, Guangxin Xue, Henrik Junge, Sergey Sergeyev, Matthias Beller, Bert U. W. Maes

Hydrogen borrowing (HB) enables sustainable C–N, C–C, and C–S bond formation using alcohols as alkylating agents. Heterogeneous HB catalysts offer improved recyclability and scalability (continuous production).

DOI: 10.1039/d3cs00314k

item.title: MOFs for photonics: bridging photocatalysis, optical wireless communication, and high-energy radiation sensing
item.description:
Authors: Jian-Xin Wang, Osama Shekhah, Gurwinder Singh, Ajayan Vinu, Mohamed Eddaoudi, Omar F. Mohammed

Light-conversion materials hold considerable promise for addressing global energy and environmental challenges, with applications spanning photocatalysis, optical wireless communication (OWC), and high-energy photon detection and imaging.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01233g

item.title: Non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals: from rational synthesis to mechanism insight for advanced electrocatalysis
item.description:
Authors: Yu Wang, Qing Liu, Qihao Wang, Jing Li, Tianyi Ma, Weiping Xiao, Zhongyong Yuan, Zexing Wu, Lei Wang

This review presents the recently developed non-carbon-supported low-loading precious metals for various key energy conversion reactions.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00046k

item.title: Recent advances in multicolor inorganic persistent luminescent materials: mechanisms, properties, and applications
item.description:
Authors: Yuhua Wang, Xilin Ma, Hongzhe Zhang, Yujie Peng

We illustrate the physical pictures, performance evaluation criteria, and microscopic mechanisms of persistent luminescence, and further highlight the application-oriented multicolor design principles of inorganic persistent luminescent materials.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00472e

item.title: Regulating glycerol electrooxidation pathways via catalytic environments
item.description:
Authors: Yabo Qi, Hanzhi Ye, Shouxin Liu, Hui Luo, Hongwu Chen, Maria-Magdalena Titirici

A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00908e

item.title: Liquid metal biomimetics: a chemical perspective
item.description:
Authors: Caiyi Liu, Jianye Gao, Yibing Ma, Jinze Li, Xiangyu Zhou, Minghui Guo, Jing Liu

A chemistry-centered framework for Ga-based liquid metal biomimetics, linking multiscale material design and interfacial reactions to matter simulation, energy conversion, information processing and cross-habitat adaptation.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00623j

item.title: Small-molecule RGB emitters for organic light-emitting diodes: a focus on device operational lifetime
item.description:
Authors: Pei Zhao, Hai-Yan Lu, Chuan-Feng Chen

Red, green and blue emitter performance is critical to full-color OLED display. This review highlights advances in RGB OLEDs based on fluorescent, phosphorescent, and TADF small-molecule emitters, with a focus on operational stability.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00510a

item.title: Optimizing the three-phase interface in proton exchange membrane fuel cells: performance bottlenecks and regulation strategies
item.description:
Authors: Haiyang Fan, Jiaxin Li, Rui Liu, Wenxiu Yang, Xiao Feng, Bo Wang

A TPB-centered framework reveals how coupled oxygen, proton, and water transport, together with ionomer-induced interfacial effects, govern PEMFC cathode performance.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs00256k

Anions as catalysts: from organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles to base-embedding electrophiles

Anions are efficient catalysts when combined with organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles or with base-embedding electrophiles, the latter is an emerging catalytic deprotonation strategy which disentangles turnover from acidity–basicity constraints.

item.title: Potassium-ion batteries for stationary energy storage solutions
item.description:
Authors: Rizwan Ur Rehman Sagar, Wei Zhang, Shaoming Huang, Ying Ian Chen

Potassium-ion batteries are a potentially sustainable and cost-competitive technology for large-scale stationary energy storage.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cs01228k

item.title: Chemistry-transforming applications of artificial intelligence
item.description:
Authors: Michael G. Medvedev, Nikita S. Serov, Vasily A. Chaliy, Egor A. Ilin, Ilya V. Prolomov, Maria A. Eremeyeva, Mark Yu. Schneider, Igor A. Mezentsev, Daniil V. Artamonov, Daniil A. Boiko, Vladimir V. Vanovskiy, Alexander A. Ryabov, Evgeny V. Burnaev, Valentine P. Ananikov

item.title: C–H⋯X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks: assembly, structural characteristics and emerging applications
item.description:
Authors: Zhen Yuan, Zhile Xiong, Liangji Chen, Zhiliang Jin, Hai Liu, Shengchang Xiang, Banglin Chen, Zhangjing Zhang

Weak yet cooperative C–H⋯X hydrogen bonds support C–H···X hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks. This Review summarizes their assembly, structural regulation, representative applications, and future challenges.
